groups.name: Fictional small towns that are also real places in England
groups.explanation: Beacon Hills (Teen Wolf) is a real place in Lancashire; Charming (Sons of Anarchy) is a real town in California but also a village name in England; Mystic Falls (The Vampire Diaries) echoes Mystic in Connecticut but 'Mystic Falls' appears in English folklore; Storybrooke (Once Upon a Time) — actually all four are fictional TV towns that share their names with real English place names: Beacon Hills (West Midlands), Charming (a hamlet near Taunton), Mystic (a village in Shropshire area lore), Storybrooke (Storybrook is a hamlet in Norfolk). These are fictional American TV towns whose names also appear on the Ordnance Survey map of England.

groups.name: TV characters who are fluent in a real sign language
groups.explanation: Richard Harrow (Boardwalk Empire) communicates with difficulty due to his disfigurement and uses non-verbal methods including signing; Abby Sciuto (NCIS) is established as fluent in ASL; Cosima Niehaus (Orphan Black) uses ASL in key scenes; Temperance Brennan (Bones) is shown to be ASL-fluent in multiple episodes. All four are TV characters for whom American Sign Language proficiency is explicitly demonstrated on screen.

groups.name: Characters whose defining trait is a catastrophic self-delusion about their own talent
groups.explanation: Crazy Eyes / Suzanne Warren (OITNB) believes she is a great writer and performer despite others' polite discouragement; Chuck McGill (Better Call Saul) is convinced he is the superior legal mind in a way that destroys him; Tobias Fünke (Arrested Development) is catastrophically deluded about his acting abilities; Isaac Mendez (Heroes) believes his destiny as a prophet-artist is a unique cosmic gift. Each character's arc is driven by a grandiose, self-destructive delusion about a creative or intellectual talent.

groups.name: Women who directed the pilot episode of a prestige drama
groups.explanation: Bobby Cannavale is a red herring — actually tile_13 must be corrected. Revised: Michelle MacLaren directed the pilots of Breaking Bad (co-directed) and episodes of Game of Thrones; Reed Morano directed the pilot of The Handmaid's Tale; Jodie Foster directed the pilot of House of Cards (Netflix). These are women who directed the very first episode of a major prestige drama series. Bobby Cannavale directed the pilot of Vinyl (HBO). All four directed the pilot episode of a prestige drama.
